cross_source_observations: Inventories identify relevance by keyword and path; several high-value items are merely candidates and were not read. In particular, mblode's chat-history skill/references, wshobson's standup command, sentimony attribution guidance, Superpowers session discovery, Anthropic/ECC session and email material need follow-up before design claims.
The named commit-only skill assumes current git email identifies the author. That does not establish identity across GitHub, Jira, Slack, or agent accounts and cannot include non-commit work.

The reviewed sources often use modification/update time, rolling recent windows, or current status. Reports need to define event time per artifact type (merge/close/review/send/incident-resolution/message timestamp) and retain update/fetch timestamps separately; this recommendation is a synthesis, not a source rule.

A handoff or incident record can include activity by an on-call role/team. Require explicit user/actor participation before attributing it personally; keep observed incident status separate from the user's action.

No reviewed source demonstrates a complete source connector contract, robust cross-source deduplication, work vs open-source classification, or calendar-month/week boundaries. These remain design requirements from the brief, not borrowed precedents.
The user requires report plus detail subfiles; sources support durable artifacts and citations but none reviewed define an HTML package with useful self-contained follow-up evidence.

Expanded screening adds concrete provider and source semantics: Cursor README files describe Gmail/Outlook and Google/Outlook Calendar plugin transports but setup alone is not proof of current connection; Slack and email have stable source IDs and explicit read/write capability behavior in Compound source contracts; Cursor Notion/Slack/Linear references emphasize full thread/page/ticket context and retention/access gaps.

Event reports should keep original event timestamp and source update/fetch time apart. Compound email uses received-time cursor and RFC Message-ID; Slack uses message ts and per-reply IDs; Jira/Linear fields can have later updates, and GSD tracks completed_at. These are different event semantics, not interchangeable timestamps.

Agent session discovery needs identity confirmation beyond recency and must separate human messages, injected content, tool outputs, and dispatch prompts (Superpowers session-discovery lines 12-25). Detailed raw logs can be retained only as a private, optional evidence layer; GSD activity-log explicitly calls raw dumps debug artifacts.

Commitments can be represented as pending obligations only when source evidence names an owner/action or clear user commitment. Jira/meeting action extraction and email thread commitment checks supply candidate signals; assigning a third-party task or team incident to the user from mere attendance/assignment context remains unsupported.

adopted_design: Codex Luna extraction for every available source/workstream, including CLI-collected sources.
Complete metric metadata separated from relevance summaries; primary verifies material claims.
Action-time half-open windows, verified actor roles and canonical identities.
Public employer repositories belong to work; unknown classification remains visible.
Distinct historical activity and current obligations with older unresolved backlog.
Retained minimal excerpts and exact locators, not full transcripts or raw mailboxes.
Deterministic validation, deduplication, counts, date resolution and static HTML rendering.
rejected_or_changed: No calendar attendance/hours from an accepted invite.
No primary-only or other-model fallback when the user required Luna.
No Jira/Linear current-status field or aggregate query count as proof of historical personal closures.
Do not collapse different review/merge events merely because they share a PR URL.
Do not adopt Compound five-session/branch relevance caps as complete month coverage.
No mandatory standup interview, Slack posting, email sending, scheduling or automatic installation.
Do not infer work ownership from repository visibility or any arbitrary connected workspace.
No broad new SDK client framework or vendored transcript parser.

Meeting metadata/notes/transcript tools and access constraints; docs differ from newer integration scope, so runtime capability is authoritative.
